policy: A dated source proving the existence of a fort does not certify the exact geospatial boundary of the fort. Modern archaeological statutory outer geometry must not be represented as historical English-held political area.

findings.source: RCAHMS/HES site history references Hertford inspection of old Roxburgh castle in 1545
findings.what_is_supported: Hertford examined the castle, reported it ruined; later 1547 works attested
findings.what_is_not_supported: This 1545 reconnaissance does not prove English artillery garrison control of the c110x65m 1547-built fort
findings.cartography: no 1545 new English artillery fort polygon

findings.source: RCAHMS 1956 inventory and HES site survey 2006–2009; 1547 Lord Grey letter
findings.what_is_supported: 1547-10-15 contemporaneous fort plan; GIS interpreted c110x65m English enclosure amid larger medieval ridge
findings.what_is_not_supported: Maximal measurements are not digitized fort polygon vertices, and main earthwork ditch may predate Tudor forts
findings.cartography: verified garrison reference point + modern archaeological extent dashed; no historic solid Polygon

findings.source: East Lothian study gazetteer references SM3191 and English artillery fort in the Haddington campaign
findings.what_is_supported: Surviving ramparts and deep ditches enclose a triangular area on the plateau, in the 1548-49 English fort; nearby gazebo dated early 18c is distinct
findings.what_is_not_supported: The official SM3191 scheduled perimeter is NOT a dated 1548 surveyed bastion trace. Later landscaping cannot be assumed Tudor
findings.cartography: modern legal scheduled polygon as unfilled dashed archaeology reference; historically bounded fort still needs footprint separation

findings.source: Ordnance Survey County Name Books, Oldhamstocks (ScotlandsPeople)
findings.what_is_supported: The label 'French Camp' existed as a later place name beside Summerhouse Hill
findings.what_is_not_supported: French Camp toponym does not prove the 1548 fort was occupied by French troops

findings.what_is_supported: 1547 English garrison to summer 1550, then French 1557 additions; excavation investigated both distinct fort phases
findings.what_is_not_supported: 1557 BL Cotton spy drawing depicts later French phase and cannot be used as English 1547 plan
findings.cartography: two phase-specific layer candidate; historic English 1547 polygon needs first-phase plan

findings.source: SCAPE/Eyemouth Museum & St Andrews Open Virtual Worlds 1557 project
findings.what_is_supported: Later 1557 rampart/ditch archaeological remains and virtual interpretation existed
findings.what_is_not_supported: 2010s virtual 1557 French fort image is a model, not measured 1547 English fort footprint
findings.cartography: no direct historic 1547 polygon derived from VR

next_archive_actions.verification: geometry demonstrably 1547, not modern SM1718; expert-reviewed and reuse rights
